label: Maya (teacher → researcher)
tagline: Two decades of pivots — teacher, analyst, design researcher — threaded by relentless reading.

entries.title: First classroom
entries.body: First teaching job: 28 fourth-graders, one leaking ceiling, endless energy. I finished reading three novels this month just to keep up with my students.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2006
entries.body: Year 2006: tired, grateful, still reading every night before sleep.

entries.title: Classroom storytelling
entries.body: Learned to teach fractions through stories. Finished reading a stack of middle-grade books for read-alouds.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2007
entries.body: Year 2007: a pivot year. I journaled through the fear and finished reading more than I planned.

entries.title: Why kids reread
entries.body: Research note: children re-read favourites for mastery. Reading the same chapter aloud five times proved it. Finished two education books this winter.

entries.title: Book club with Lena
entries.body: Monthly book club started. We finished reading a novel a month, no exceptions. Lena keeps the list honest.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2008
entries.body: Year 2008: family first, work second, books always. Finished the year mid-novel as usual.

entries.title: Loan payoff plan
entries.body: Student loan payoff spreadsheet: seven years if nothing breaks. Reading personal-finance books at night and actually finishing them helps.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2009
entries.body: Year 2009: learned something hard, kept the book club, kept going.

entries.title: Burnout winter
entries.body: I cried in the supply closet twice this term. Something has to pivot. I love the kids; the system is eating me.

entries.title: Pivot: learn data
entries.body: Decided to pivot toward education data. Finished reading a statistics primer cover to cover. Nightschool starts January.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2010
entries.body: Year 2010: tired, grateful, still reading every night before sleep.

entries.title: Excel, then Python
entries.body: Picked up Python after Excel hit its limits. Finished reading the docs like a novel. First script cleaned a whole term of grades.

entries.title: Reading logs study
entries.body: Tracked my reading: 41 books finished this year. Reading is how I metabolise stress. Book club is now twice monthly.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2011
entries.body: Year 2011: a pivot year. I journaled through the fear and finished reading more than I planned.

entries.title: Marco, properly
entries.body: Marco Reyes from book club asked me out between chapters. We finished reading the same poetry collection and argued happily.

entries.title: Anxiety, named
entries.body: Therapy started. Naming the anxiety made it smaller. Morning pages, finished daily, keep the spiral visible.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2012
entries.body: Year 2012: family first, work second, books always. Finished the year mid-novel as usual.

entries.title: Quit teaching
entries.body: Resigned in January, mid-year, terrified. Pivot number two. The kids wrote me a book of letters; I have read it four times.

entries.title: Edtech internship
entries.body: Unpaid edtech internship at 29, humbling. Finished reading every onboarding doc in week one. Hunger beats pedigree.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2013
entries.body: Year 2013: learned something hard, kept the book club, kept going.

entries.title: Data tells stories
entries.body: Finding: attendance data predicted dropout better than grades. Reading the raw notes mattered more than the dashboard.

entries.title: Freelance famine
entries.body: Freelance data gigs, feast or famine. Three clients, one late payer. Spreadsheet and I are close now.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2014
entries.body: Year 2014: tired, grateful, still reading every night before sleep.

entries.title: Married Marco
entries.body: Small wedding, library venue obviously. We finished reading our vows from index cards. Lena officiated, cried first.

entries.title: D3 and dashboards
entries.body: Learned D3 for a client dashboard. Reading documentation cover-to-cover is still my superpower.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2015
entries.body: Year 2015: a pivot year. I journaled through the fear and finished reading more than I planned.

entries.title: Pivot: design research
entries.body: Dashboards inform but do not persuade. Pivoting toward design research: interviews, stories, evidence with faces.

entries.title: Interview craft
entries.body: Finished reading three research-methods books. Ran 20 parent interviews. Listening is a learnable skill.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2016
entries.body: Year 2016: family first, work second, books always. Finished the year mid-novel as usual.

entries.title: Migraines and screens
entries.body: Migraines traced to screen marathons. Paper books after nine. Actually finished more reading once screens dimmed.

entries.title: Laid off
entries.body: The startup folded in a week. Severance, shock, then a strange calm. I have pivoted before; I know the first steps now.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2017
entries.body: Year 2017: learned something hard, kept the book club, kept going.

entries.title: Independent consulting
entries.body: Design research consulting, first client a literacy nonprofit. Full circle: reading, data, and classrooms in one job.

entries.title: Parents read the room
entries.body: Finding: parents judge schools in the first 90 seconds of a visit. Reading body language beat survey scores.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2018
entries.body: Year 2018: tired, grateful, still reading every night before sleep.

entries.title: Read-aloud research sprints
entries.body: Method: pair every dataset with a read-aloud story session. Stakeholders remember stories; shipped as my signature workshop.

entries.title: Aunt Clara moves in
entries.body: Aunt Clara moved nearby after her fall. Sunday lunches now, three generations arguing about books.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2019
entries.body: Year 2019: a pivot year. I journaled through the fear and finished reading more than I planned.

entries.title: Lockdown library
entries.body: Pandemic spring: our flat became a library, office, and school for the neighbours kids. Finished reading 12 novels by June.

entries.title: Long walks, audiobooks
entries.body: Daily walks with audiobooks finished what paper started. Anxiety quieter. Reading while moving counts.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2020
entries.body: Year 2020: family first, work second, books always. Finished the year mid-novel as usual.

entries.title: Fiction writing, badly
entries.body: Started writing fiction at 5am. Terrible and joyful. Finished reading two craft books to suffer better.

entries.title: Pivot: research lead
entries.body: Aiming for research lead within two years. The thread through every pivot: helping people read their own story clearly.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2021
entries.body: Year 2021: learned something hard, kept the book club, kept going.

entries.title: Agency offer
entries.body: Research lead offer from a design agency. Reading the contract twice, slowly, was the whole negotiation strategy.

entries.title: House deposit
entries.body: Deposit saved. Seven years of spreadsheets. Marco framed the first payoff chart next to our bookshelf.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2022
entries.body: Year 2022: tired, grateful, still reading every night before sleep.

entries.title: Synthesis walls
entries.body: Method: physical synthesis walls, every interview a card, patterns you can touch. Teams finished reading the wall before the deck.

entries.title: Book club at ten years
entries.body: Book club turned ten. 118 books finished together. Lena cried; Marco baked; I just kept reading faces.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2023
entries.body: Year 2023: a pivot year. I journaled through the fear and finished reading more than I planned.

entries.title: Mama Rosa ill
entries.body: Mum hospitalised in February. Hospital waiting rooms: I finished reading three novels holding her hand between chapters.

entries.title: Grief and attention
entries.body: Finding from my own notes: grief fragments attention for months. Reading in short chapters is a kindness, not a compromise.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2024
entries.body: Year 2024: family first, work second, books always. Finished the year mid-novel as usual.

entries.title: Mentoring researchers
entries.body: Mentoring four junior researchers. I lend books aggressively and track who finishes reading them. Most do.

entries.title: Strong at 43
entries.body: Strength training twice weekly. Sleep protected. The reading chair now has a kettlebell beside it. Balance, literally.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2025
entries.body: Year 2025: learned something hard, kept the book club, kept going.

entries.title: It threads together
entries.body: Teacher, analyst, researcher, writer-in-progress. None of it was linear and all of it was reading people carefully. It works out.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2026
entries.body: Year 2026: tired, grateful, still reading every night before sleep.

entries.title: Notion export: first research notebook (2008)
entries.body: Exported page from an early notebook: close reading notes on three novels, margin questions in the margins, and a finished chapter summary for the book club. Reading slowly is the method.

entries.title: Drive export: thesis chapter draft (2010)
entries.body: Google Docs export, chapter two draft with Lena Cruz comments in the margin: tighten the claim, cite the classroom evidence, finish the literature review before August.

entries.title: Gmail thread: Marco Reyes job lead (2012)
entries.body: Email thread from Marco Reyes with a research-assistant posting, two time slots for a call, and a promise to introduce the hiring lead. Replied the same evening.

entries.title: Calendar export: book club Sundays (2014)
entries.body: Recurring calendar block, first Sunday monthly: book club with Ana Reyes and Priya Nair. Finished two novels this quarter; the shelf still grows faster in spring.

entries.title: Apple Health export summary (2015)
entries.body: Health export: StepCount records most days, sleep averaging 6h50m in May. Morning walks on teaching days show up as the steadiest activity pattern.

entries.title: Drive export: household budget sheet (2016)
entries.body: Spreadsheet export of the household budget: rent, groceries, and a book-buying line that needs its own category. Subscriptions reviewed and two cancelled.

entries.title: Slack export: #reading-circle thread (2017)
entries.body: Thread with Grace Liu: the teardown checklist earned three saved replies. Specific, short posts ending in one question keep earning conversations.

entries.title: GitHub export: reading-notes template (2018)
entries.body: Repo README for a personal reading-notes template: one question per book, margin annotations first, finished-date always recorded. Shared with two colleagues.

entries.title: LinkedIn export: Sofia Lindqvist connection (2019)
entries.body: New connection after the portfolio review night. Sofia Lindqvist researches learning design; follow up when the case-study draft is ready.

entries.title: X export: bookmarked threads (2020)
entries.body: Bookmarked threads on annotation practice and marginalia: saved twelve examples for the methods file. Public notes compound; drafts do not.

entries.title: Family export: Mama Rosa care rota (2021)
entries.body: Shared family document: Sunday lunch rota, pharmacy runs, and who drives Mama Rosa to appointments. Updated weekly by three households.

entries.title: Contacts export: Priya Nair card (2022)
entries.body: Contact card: Priya Nair, product designer, prefers email, birthday in March. Coffee every few weeks since 2014.

entries.title: Notion export: research leadership plan (2023)
entries.body: Goal page: lead a small research team within two years, mentor junior researchers, publish the annotation method. Reviewed quarterly against the calendar.

entries.title: Gmail export: clinic results letter (2024)
entries.body: Clinic letter received by email: blood pressure stable, vitamin D low, recheck in six months. Filed with the health export the same day.

entries.title: Drive export: annotation study results (2025)
entries.body: Findings doc: readers who annotated in the margins finished more books and recalled more after a month. Margin notes beat highlights on every delayed test.

entries.title: Slack export: design-friends crit (2026)
entries.body: Crit night thread with Ana Reyes: lead with the constraint, cut the second exploration, name the tradeoff. Next crit in two weeks.
